teaser.en: An acacia with powdery green-white or orange bark, and on some trees, swollen ant galls that whistle in the wind.

summary.en: *Chigundi* is a thorny, flat-topped savanna acacia known for its powdery, coloured bark and fluffy yellow flowers. Across East Africa it gives firewood, fodder and an edible gum.

about.en: *Acacia seyal* (now often called *Vachellia seyal*) is a thorny tree up to about 10 m tall with an open, flat crown when mature. Its bark is distinctive: powdery, greenish-white to pale green or orange-red. The straight white thorns grow in pairs and can reach 8 cm. In one variety some thorns swell at the base into hollow galls lived in by ants, and wind blowing across the holes makes them whistle. The fluffy flower balls are bright yellow and fragrant, and the pods are narrow, curved and light brown.

where.en: It is a typical savanna acacia, found widely from West Africa to Egypt and south to Zimbabwe. In Kenya it grows in bushed grassland and woodland, especially on seasonally flooded plains and black-cotton soils.

uses.en: ICRAF records that across Kenya the tree is used for firewood, charcoal, poles and posts, and its leaves, pods and flowers feed goats and camels. It produces a clear, edible gum that is sold, and its thorny branches make dead fences. Its bark has been used for medicine, tea, tannin and dye. Pakia records no Digo use.

names.en: Pakia records *chigundi*, with the English names 'white galled acacia' and 'whistling thorn tree'. ICRAF gives the Swahili name *mgunga* and the English 'white-thorn acacia'. *Mgunga* is also the Digo name Pakia gives to another acacia, *Acacia stuhlmannii*. Mgombato has a similar name, *chigundi-gundi*, but for a different tree, the Egyptian thorn (*Acacia nilotica*).

reason.en: Coast whistling thorn, another gall acacia

taxon.note: Acacia seyal is now Vachellia seyal

sources: Maundu, P. & Tengnäs, B. (eds) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF — sheet Acacia seyal: https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Acacia_seyal_KEN.pdf
